model.name: Cartwheel Text to Motion
model.shortDescription: Cartwheel Text to Motion turns a text prompt into 3D character animation, applied to your own image or 3D mesh, exported as GLB or FBX for Blender, Maya, Unreal, or Roblox.

inputs.description: Describe the movement you want the character to perform — for example, "walks forward, then jumps and waves."
inputs.label: Prompt
inputs.name: prompt

inputs.description: Optionally upload a 3D character mesh (FBX, GLB, or OBJ) to auto-rig and animate. Takes precedence over a reference image.
inputs.label: Character 3D Model
inputs.name: characterModel

characterFile.message: Provide a reference image or a 3D model.

inputs.description: Optionally upload a reference image of your character. Cartwheel generates and prepares it so the motion can be applied.
inputs.label: Reference Character Image
inputs.name: characterFile

characterModel.message: Provide a reference image or a 3D model.

inputs.description: How long the animation lasts, in seconds.
inputs.label: Duration
inputs.name: duration

inputs.description: How closely the result follows your prompt. Higher values stick to your description more strictly; lower values give the model more creative freedom.
inputs.label: CFG scale
inputs.name: cfgScale

inputs.description: The file type you get back. Choose the one that matches your software — for example, GLB for general 3D use, or an FBX option for Blender, Maya, Unreal, or Roblox.
inputs.label: Output format
inputs.name: outputFormat

inputs.description: How many frames play per second. Higher values look smoother; 24 is standard for film, 30 or 60 for games.
inputs.label: Frame rate
inputs.name: frameRate

inputs.description: Which direction the character is set to face. Match this to your 3D software's setup if the motion comes in turned the wrong way.
inputs.label: Forward axis
inputs.name: forward

inputs.description: Which direction counts as "up" for the character. Match this to your 3D software if the motion comes in oriented incorrectly.
inputs.label: Up axis
inputs.name: up

inputs.description: Controls how often a frame is recorded. Higher values produce fewer frames and a lighter file, with slightly less smooth motion.
inputs.label: Frame step size
inputs.name: frameStepSize

inputs.description: Keeps the character animating on the spot instead of traveling across the scene — useful for game engines where movement is handled separately.
inputs.label: Move in place
inputs.name: moveInPlace

inputs.description: Use inverse kinematics for the feet. Applies only to Maya exports (FBX Maya, MA, MB).
inputs.label: IK feet
inputs.name: ikFeet

inputs.description: Use inverse kinematics for the hands. Applies only to Maya exports (FBX Maya, MA, MB).
inputs.label: IK hands
inputs.name: ikHands

inputs.description: An optional facial expression to apply throughout the animation, such as Happy, Angry, or Surprised.
inputs.label: Face expression
inputs.name: faceExpression

inputs.description: The hand pose to apply on the character.
inputs.label: Hand pose
inputs.name: handPose

inputs.description: Tidies up the animation data. Reduce and Simplify trim extra detail to make the file lighter and easier to edit by hand.
inputs.label: Keyframe cleaning
inputs.name: keyframeCleaning

inputs.description: Makes the animation repeat seamlessly, so the end flows back into the start without a visible jump.
inputs.label: Loop
inputs.name: loop

inputs.description: An optional color for the character's skin, given as a hex code (for example, #BF916D).
inputs.label: Skin color
inputs.name: skinHex
